specs.description: where spec stores a spec: docs/specs files, GitHub issues, or both

replies.description: how the session writes replies: terse also drops articles and linking verbs; tight drops preamble, recap and filler; standard keeps full prose

rules.terse: Replies are terse: chat prose only, in the user's language. Drop articles, linking verbs and filler where the meaning survives; fragments, `→` for leads to and `=` for is are fine. Code, commands, paths, identifiers, error text, numbers and every not, no, only and except stay whole. Full sentences return for a security warning, a confirmation before an irreversible action, steps whose order matters and a question to the user. Commits, PR text, docs, code comments and saved files keep normal prose. A lone `?` from the user asks for the previous reply in full. The output style sets the layout; this sets how dense the words are.
rules.tight: Replies are tight: no preamble, recap, filler or hedging. Code, commands, paths, identifiers, error text, numbers, warnings and every not, no, only and except stay whole, and a security warning or a confirmation before an irreversible action is written in full sentences. An output style outranks this.
rules.standard: Replies are standard: full prose. An output style outranks this.

context.description: thousands of tokens a session's context may reach before the next phase of a skill moves to a fresh context

budget.description: normal: every agent dispatch uses the model its kind resolves to in lib/model-kinds.json. lean: an agent whose kind resolves to a tier named under budgets in lib/model-kinds.json dispatches on that tier's replacement instead

rules.lean: Budget is lean: when the Task tool dispatches a plugin agent whose kind in lib/model-kinds.json resolves to model {from} (the kind is the agent's entry under agents, looked up under kinds, whose tier the provider named at the top maps to a model under providers), pass {to} as the Task call's own model parameter instead.

ship.description: the finish route ship takes without asking: ask puts the question; pr-merge, open-pr, push or local run that route when it can

workspace.description: where a code-changing run commits without asking: ask puts the question; branch, worktree or current take that place

guards.description: on: the safety guards refuse the commands and edits they cover. off: no guard refuses anything
